quarterly_data.quarter: SiTime Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: First disclosure of SiTime's optical-module share by generation and of the 3.2T pipeline. Vashist: 'Overall, the optical module business in a couple of years is probably $0.5 billion for us. It's big. It's very large. We joined this business in 400, where we were about 40% of the market share. In 1.6, we probably double that, close to double that. The ASPs have gone from around $1 to 40%, 50% growth... Eventually, the 3.2, which is already in design win, will probably get to be even more in market share as it gets to higher frequencies, lower jitter, greater resilience to temperature.'
quarterly_data.figure: optical module business probably $0.5 billion in a couple of years; about 40% of the market share at 400, close to double at 1.6; 3.2 already in design win

quarterly_data.quarter: SiTime Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Per-socket and per-rack timing content quantified by CFO Beth Howe: 'Switches, you have multiple chips with typically maybe $20, $25 worth of content in the typical switch. Our ASPs range from $1 to $2 at the low end to $4 to $7, up to $10 for certain higher end oscillators. The clock ASPs run in the typically $4, $6 kind of range... As you build those up into racks, you can see multiple hundreds of dollars worth of content in racks and sometimes up to over $1,000 of timing content in certain rack configurations.' Vashist described the attach points: 'We are in the GPU, the TPU, the CPU. We are along with the switches. We are sitting next to the NIC cards. We are in the smart cables. We are in the pluggable optical modules.' Customer set spans optical/transceiver vendors, hyperscalers, neo clouds, sovereigns, other semiconductor providers and OEMs.
quarterly_data.figure: $20, $25 of content in the typical switch; oscillator ASPs $1 to $2 up to $10; clock ASPs $4, $6; up to over $1,000 of timing content in certain rack configurations

quarterly_data.quarter: SiTime Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: SAM re-sizing. Data center: 'When we went public... there was a data center business which was around $800 million in SAM. Today, that would be probably close to $3 billion in SAM opportunity.' Total timing TAM: 'when you think of timing TAM, we see it doubling almost between now, $12 billion, $11 billion, by the end of the decade, which is faster than we would've expected. We would normally expect it to do that in seven, eight, 10 years, but we think it's going to happen in the next four or five years.' Asked about the moderator's $25 billion by 2030 framing, Vashist answered 'Give or take. Could be a little bit less, maybe 22 or so, but significantly higher', tying it to semis going 'from $700 billion... to, pick a number, $1.6 trillion to $2 trillion'. Under-penetrated pockets called out: sovereign data centers, enterprise data centers and Chinese data centers.
quarterly_data.figure: data center SAM around $800 million at IPO to close to $3 billion today; timing TAM $12 billion, $11 billion doubling by the end of the decade (maybe 22 or so)

quarterly_data.quarter: SiTime Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Timing moving from discrete components into the package, quantified and dated for the first time. Vashist on chiplets, substrates and modules: 'that can be rather large. We think it could be anything from a billion to 1.5 billion more of SAM. The reason for all of this, of course, is because timing needs to get closer, timing needs to get more clean, the signal needs to be less attenuated, and just like in power, you have VPD, vertical delivery, we think there's a concept called VTD, which is getting closer and closer to the chip, either below, embedded in the substrate or above. I think that this could start as early as 2028, maybe 2029.' He called it 'mostly incremental' rather than cannibalistic because it lands at the very high end.
quarterly_data.figure: a billion to 1.5 billion more of SAM; could start as early as 2028, maybe 2029

quarterly_data.quarter: SiTime Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Forward growth rate for the acquired Renesas Timing Products Division, a step beyond the Q3-only guidance given on the August call. Vashist: 'It's had a tremendous clock growth, and that growth, I think, continues... I think it's also fair to say that next year is probably very similar to that growth rate of well above 50%, maybe in the 60%, 70%, even 80% range for that TPD business. That is, by the way, without that much help from SiTime.' Cross-selling is already opening doors: TPD 'dragged us into very large organizations where we didn't have much penetration in the hyperscalers, one of the large hyperscalers', and SiTime is taking TPD into chip companies it had not penetrated. Sales force 'about 100 people exiting this year'; TPD's roadmap goes from one or two products a year to 'three, four, five products coming out'.
quarterly_data.figure: TPD growth next year well above 50%, maybe in the 60%, 70%, even 80% range; sales force about 100 people exiting this year

quarterly_data.quarter: SiTime Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Two supply datapoints. (1) The clock/TPD business is supply-constrained, not demand-constrained: 'if we could get more product in the supply chain, that's one place where we are constrained working through Renesas and the TSAs, we could probably be significantly higher than that number.' (2) MEMS wafer supply from Bosch is not a concern — 'it is not in my top 20 things to worry about. Bosch has been a partner of SiTime since 2007... We are the only MEMS non-Bosch company there. In other words, they are a captive fab. They are not supposed to be merchant fab.' On renewal: 'I fully expect that as our 2027 10-year deal with them sort of comes off, there will be another one that will extend the time.'
quarterly_data.figure: constrained working through Renesas and the TSAs; Bosch 2027 10-year deal expected to be extended
